title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purpose of protecting and improving the environment, preventing and controlling air pollution, safeguarding public health, promoting ecological civilization, and advancing sustainable economic and social development.

Article 2 The prevention and control of air pollution shall aim at improving the quality of the atmospheric environment, adhere to source control, prioritize planning, transform the economic development pattern, optimize the industrial structure and layout, and adjust the energy structure.
The prevention and control of air pollution shall strengthen comprehensive prevention and control of air pollution from coal combustion, industry, motor vehicles and vessels, dust, agriculture, etc., promote joint regional prevention and control of air pollution, and implement coordinated control of air pollutants such as particulate matter, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, ammonia, and greenhouse gases.

Article 3 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate the work of air pollution prevention and control into national economic and social development plans, and increase financial investment in air pollution prevention and control.
Local people's governments at all levels shall be responsible for the quality of the atmospheric environment within their respective administrative regions, formulate plans, take measures to control or gradually reduce the discharge of air pollutants, so that the quality of the atmospheric environment meets the prescribed standards and is gradually improved.

Article 4 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments of the State Council, assess the completion of targets for improving the quality of the atmospheric environment and key tasks for air pollution prevention and control in provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, in accordance with the provisions of the State Council. The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall formulate assessment measures and implement assessment of the completion of local targets for improving the quality of the atmospheric environment and key tasks for air pollution prevention and control within their respective administrative regions. The assessment results shall be disclosed to the public.

Article 5 The competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level shall exercise unified supervision and management over the prevention and control of air pollution.
Other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall exercise supervision and management over the prevention and control of air pollution within their respective functions and duties.

Article 6 The State encourages and supports scientific and technological research on air pollution prevention and control, conducts analysis of the sources of air pollution and their trends, promotes advanced and applicable technologies and equipment for air pollution prevention and control, facilitates the transformation of scientific and technological achievements, and gives play to the supporting role of science and technology in air pollution prevention and control.

Article 7 Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators shall take effective measures to prevent and reduce air pollution, and bear liability according to law for the damage caused.
Citizens shall enhance their awareness of atmospheric environmental protection, adopt a low-carbon and frugal lifestyle, and conscientiously fulfill their obligations to protect the atmospheric environment.

Article 8 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council or the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, when formulating atmospheric environmental quality standards, aim to safeguard public health and protect the ecological environment, adapt to economic and social development, and ensure scientific rationality.

Article 9 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council or the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, when formulating air pollutant emission standards, base them on the atmospheric environmental quality standards and the national economic and technical conditions.

Article 10 When formulating atmospheric environmental quality standards and air pollutant emission standards, experts shall be organized to review and demonstrate them, and opinions shall be solicited from relevant departments, industry associations, enterprises, public institutions, and the public.

Article 11 The competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall publish on its website the atmospheric environmental quality standards and air pollutant emission standards for the public to consult and download free of charge.

Article 12 The implementation of atmospheric environmental quality standards and air pollutant emission standards shall be evaluated regularly, and the standards shall be revised in a timely manner based on the evaluation results.

Article 13 When formulating quality standards for coal, petroleum coke, biomass fuels, coatings and other products containing volatile organic compounds, fireworks and firecrackers, boilers and other products, the requirements for the protection of the atmospheric environment shall be clearly specified.
When formulating fuel quality standards, the national air pollutant control requirements shall be met, and they shall be coordinated with and implemented simultaneously with the national air pollutant emission standards for motor vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery.
For the purpose of the preceding paragraph, 'non-road mobile machinery' means mobile machinery and transportable industrial equipment equipped with engines.

Article 14 The people's government of a city that fails to meet the national atmospheric environmental quality standards shall promptly formulate a plan for achieving the standards within a time limit, take measures, and achieve the atmospheric environmental quality standards within the time limit prescribed by the State Council or the provincial people's government.
When formulating a plan for achieving the standards within a time limit for a city, opinions shall be solicited from relevant industry associations, enterprises, public institutions, experts, and the public.

Article 15 The plan for achieving the standards within a time limit for a city's atmospheric environmental quality shall be disclosed to the public. The plans for achieving the standards within a time limit for municipalities directly under the Central Government and cities divided into districts shall be submitted to the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council for recordation.

Article 16 When annually reporting on the environmental conditions and the completion of environmental protection targets to the people's congress or its standing committee at the same level, the city people's government shall report on the implementation of the plan for achieving the standards within a time limit for the city's atmospheric environmental quality, and shall disclose it to the public.

Article 17 The plan for achieving the standards within a time limit for a city's atmospheric environmental quality shall be evaluated and revised in a timely manner based on the requirements for air pollution prevention and control and economic and technical conditions.

Article 18 Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators constructing projects that have an impact on the atmospheric environment shall conduct environmental impact assessments according to law and disclose the environmental impact assessment documents; those that discharge pollutants into the atmosphere shall comply with the air pollutant emission standards and abide by the requirements for total discharge control of key air pollutants.

Article 19 Enterprises, public institutions that discharge industrial waste gas or toxic and harmful air pollutants listed in the catalogue specified in Article 78 of this Law, coal-fired heat source production and operation units of centralized heating facilities, and other units subject to pollutant discharge permit management according to law shall obtain pollutant discharge permits. The specific measures and implementation steps for pollutant discharge permits shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 20 Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators that discharge pollutants into the atmosphere shall install air pollutant discharge outlets in accordance with laws, regulations, and the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.
It is prohibited to discharge air pollutants by evading supervision through means such as illegal discharge, tampering with or fabricating monitoring data, temporary suspension of production for the purpose of evading on-site inspection, opening emergency discharge channels under non-emergency circumstances, or abnormal operation of air pollution prevention and control facilities.

Article 21 The State implements total discharge control of key air pollutants.
The total discharge control targets for key air pollutants shall, after soliciting opinions from the relevant departments of the State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, be submitted by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council together with the comprehensive economic department under the State Council to the State Council for approval and issuance for implementation.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in accordance with the total discharge control targets issued by the State Council, control or reduce the total discharge of key air pollutants within their respective administrative regions.
The specific measures for determining total discharge control targets and allocating total discharge control indicators shall be prescribed by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council together with the relevant departments of the State Council. The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the needs of air pollution prevention and control within their respective administrative regions, implement total discharge control for air pollutants other than the national key air pollutants.
The State shall gradually promote the trading of emission rights for key air pollutants.

Article 22 For areas that exceed the national total discharge control targets for key air pollutants or fail to achieve the targets for improving the quality of the atmospheric environment assigned by the State, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall, together with the relevant departments, interview the principal responsible persons of the people's government of the area, and suspend the approval of environmental impact assessment documents for construction projects that would increase the total discharge of key air pollutants in that area. The interview situation shall be disclosed to the public.

Article 23 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall be responsible for formulating monitoring and evaluation norms for atmospheric environmental quality and air pollution sources, organizing the construction and management of a national monitoring network for atmospheric environmental quality and air pollution sources, organizing and conducting monitoring of atmospheric environmental quality and air pollution sources, and uniformly publishing information on the national atmospheric environmental quality status.
The competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for organizing the construction and management of a monitoring network for atmospheric environmental quality and air pollution sources within its administrative region, conducting monitoring of atmospheric environmental quality and air pollution sources, and uniformly publishing information on the atmospheric environmental quality status within its administrative region.

Article 24 Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and monitoring norms, monitor the industrial waste gas they discharge and the toxic and harmful air pollutants listed in the catalogue specified in Article 78 of this Law, and keep the original monitoring records. Among them, key pollutant-discharging units shall install and use automatic monitoring equipment for air pollutant discharge, connect it to the monitoring equipment of the competent department of ecological environment, ensure the normal operation of the monitoring equipment, and publicly disclose discharge information according to law. The specific measures for monitoring and the conditions for key pollutant-discharging units shall be prescribed by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.
The list of key pollutant-discharging units shall be determined by the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council, based on factors such as the atmospheric environmental carrying capacity of the administrative region, the requirements for total discharge control of key air pollutants, and the types, quantities, and concentrations of air pollutants discharged by the pollutant-discharging units, after consultation with relevant departments, and shall be published to the public.

Article 25 Key pollutant-discharging units shall be responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of the automatic monitoring data. If the competent department of ecological environment discovers anomalies in the data transmitted by the automatic monitoring equipment for air pollutant discharge from a key pollutant-discharging unit, it shall promptly conduct an investigation.

Article 26 It is prohibited to occupy, damage, or without authorization move or alter atmospheric environmental quality monitoring facilities and automatic monitoring equipment for air pollutant discharge.

Article 27 The State implements a phase-out system for technologies, equipment, and products that cause serious pollution to the atmospheric environment.
The comprehensive economic department under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments of the State Council, determine the phase-out period for technologies, equipment, and products that cause serious pollution to the atmospheric environment, and include them in the national comprehensive industrial policy catalogue.
Producers, importers, sellers, or users shall stop producing, importing, selling, or using the equipment and products listed in the catalogue specified in the preceding paragraph within the prescribed period. Adopters of technologies shall stop adopting the technologies listed in the catalogue specified in the preceding paragraph within the prescribed period.
The phased-out equipment and products shall not be transferred to others for use.

Article 28 The competent department of ecological environment under the State Council shall, together with the relevant departments, establish and improve a system for assessing damage caused by air pollution.

Article 29 The competent department of ecological environment and its environmental law enforcement agencies, as well as other departments responsible for supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection, have the right to conduct supervision and inspection of enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators that discharge air pollutants by means such as on-site inspection and monitoring, automatic monitoring, remote sensing monitoring, and far-infrared imaging. The entity being inspected shall truthfully report the situation and provide necessary information. The departments, agencies, and their staff conducting the inspection shall keep confidential the trade secrets of the entity being inspected.

Article 30 Where an enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator discharges air pollutants in violation of laws and regulations, causing or likely to cause serious air pollution, or where relevant evidence may be destroyed or concealed, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level and other departments responsible for supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection may take administrative compulsory measures such as sealing up or distraining the relevant facilities, equipment, and articles.

Article 31 The competent department of ecological environment and other departments responsible for supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection shall publish reporting telephone numbers, email addresses, etc., to facilitate public reporting.
Upon receiving a report, the competent department of ecological environment and other departments responsible for supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection shall promptly handle it and keep confidential the relevant information of the whistleblower; for a real-name report, the department shall provide feedback on the handling results, etc., and if verified, the handling results shall be publicly disclosed according to law, and the whistleblower shall be rewarded.
If a whistleblower reports the unit in which he or she works, the unit may not retaliate against the whistleblower by means such as terminating or altering the labor contract or by other means.

Article 32 The relevant departments of the State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall take measures to adjust the energy structure, promote the production and use of clean energy; optimize the use of coal, promote clean and efficient utilization of coal, gradually reduce the proportion of coal in primary energy consumption, and reduce air pollutant emissions during coal production, use, and conversion.

Article 33 The State promotes coal washing and processing to reduce the sulfur and ash content of coal, and restricts the mining of coal with high sulfur and ash content. New coal mines shall simultaneously construct supporting coal washing facilities so that the sulfur and ash content of coal meets the prescribed standards; for existing coal mines, except where the coal mined is of low sulfur and ash content or does not require washing according to the requirements of coal-fired power plants that have achieved compliant emissions, supporting coal washing facilities shall be built within a time limit.
It is prohibited to mine coal containing radioactive substances or toxic and harmful substances such as arsenic exceeding the prescribed standards.

Article 34 The State adopts economic and technical policies and measures conducive to the clean and efficient utilization of coal, and encourages and supports the development and promotion of clean coal technologies.
The State encourages coal mining enterprises and others to adopt reasonable and feasible technical measures to exploit and utilize coalbed methane and to comprehensively utilize coal gangue. Those engaged in the exploitation and utilization of coalbed methane shall ensure that the emission of coalbed methane complies with the relevant standards and norms.

Article 35 The State prohibits the import, sale, or burning of coal that does not meet quality standards, and encourages the burning of high-quality coal.
Units storing materials such as coal, coal gangue, coal slag, and coal ash shall take measures to prevent spontaneous combustion and prevent air pollution.

Article 36 Local people's governments at all levels shall take measures to strengthen the management of civil bulk coal, prohibit the sale of coal that does not meet the quality standards for civil bulk coal, encourage residents to burn high-quality coal and clean briquettes, and promote energy-saving and environmentally friendly stoves.

Article 37 Petroleum refining enterprises shall produce fuel oil in accordance with the fuel quality standards.
It is prohibited to import, sell, or burn petroleum coke that does not meet quality standards.

Article 38 City people's governments may designate and publish areas where the burning of high-pollution fuel is prohibited, and shall gradually expand the scope of such areas based on the requirements for improving the quality of the atmospheric environment. The catalogue of high-pollution fuel shall be determined by the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council.
Within the prohibited areas, the sale and burning of high-pollution fuel shall be prohibited; the construction or expansion of facilities burning high-pollution fuel shall be prohibited, and existing facilities shall be converted to use natural gas, shale gas, liquefied petroleum gas, electricity, or other clean energy within the time limit prescribed by the city people's government.

Article 39 Urban construction shall be comprehensively planned, and in areas with coal-fired heating, combined heat and power generation and centralized heating shall be promoted. In areas covered by centralized heating pipelines, the construction or expansion of decentralized coal-fired heating boilers shall be prohibited; existing coal-fired heating boilers that cannot meet emission standards shall be dismantled within the time limit prescribed by the city people's government.

Article 40 The market supervision and management department of the people's government at or above the county level shall, together with the competent department of ecological environment, conduct supervision and inspection of compliance with environmental protection standards or requirements in the production, import, sale, and use of boilers; those failing to meet the environmental protection standards or requirements shall not be produced, imported, sold, or used.

Article 41 Coal-fired power plants and other coal-fired units shall adopt clean production processes, install supporting dust removal, desulfurization, denitrification and other devices, or take other measures such as technical transformation to control air pollutant emissions.
The State encourages coal-fired units to adopt advanced technologies and devices for coordinated control of air pollutants such as dust removal, desulfurization, denitrification, and mercury removal to reduce air pollutant emissions.
Article 42 Power dispatching shall prioritize the grid connection of electricity generated from clean energy.

Article 43 Enterprises in industries such as iron and steel, building materials, non-ferrous metals, petroleum, and chemical engineering that discharge dust, sulfides, and nitrogen oxides during the production process shall adopt clean production processes, install supporting dust removal, desulfurization, denitrification and other devices, or take other measures such as technical transformation to control air pollutant emissions.

Article 44 The volatile organic compound content of raw materials and products containing volatile organic compounds that are produced, imported, sold, and used shall comply with quality standards or requirements.
The State encourages the production, import, sale, and use of low-toxicity, low-volatile organic solvents.

Article 45 Production and service activities that generate waste gas containing volatile organic compounds shall be conducted in enclosed spaces or equipment, and pollution prevention and control facilities shall be installed and used in accordance with the provisions; where enclosure is not possible, measures shall be taken to reduce waste gas emissions.

Article 46 Industrial coating enterprises shall use coatings with low volatile organic compound content, and establish records to document the usage, waste, destination, and volatile organic compound content of production raw materials and auxiliary materials. The records shall be kept for not less than three years.

Article 47 Enterprises in petroleum, chemical engineering, and other industries that produce or use organic solvents shall take measures to carry out daily maintenance and repair of pipelines and equipment, reduce material leakage, and promptly collect and treat leaked materials.
Oil and gas storage depots, gas stations, crude oil and refined oil terminals, crude oil and refined oil transportation vessels, tank trucks, and gas tank trucks, etc., shall install oil and gas recovery devices in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and maintain their normal operation.

Article 48 Enterprises in industries such as iron and steel, building materials, non-ferrous metals, petroleum, chemical engineering, pharmaceuticals, and mining shall strengthen refined management, take measures such as centralized collection and treatment, and strictly control the discharge of dust and gaseous pollutants.
Industrial production enterprises shall take measures such as enclosure, fencing, covering, cleaning, and watering to reduce the discharge of dust and gaseous pollutants from internal material storage, transfer, loading, and unloading operations.

Article 49 Combustible gas generated from industrial production, landfill, or other activities shall be recovered and utilized; where recovery and utilization are not feasible, pollution prevention and control treatment shall be carried out.
If a combustible gas recovery and utilization device cannot operate normally, it shall be repaired or replaced promptly. If it is necessary to discharge combustible gas while the recovery and utilization device is inoperative, the discharged combustible gas shall be fully combusted or other measures shall be taken to control air pollutant emissions, and the local competent department of ecological environment shall be reported, and the device shall be repaired or replaced within the required time limit.

Article 50 The State advocates low-carbon and environmentally friendly travel, rationally controls the number of fuel-powered motor vehicles based on urban planning, vigorously develops urban public transportation, and increases the proportion of public transportation trips.
The State adopts fiscal, taxation, government procurement and other measures to promote the application of energy-saving, environmentally friendly, and new energy motor vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery, limits the development of high fuel consumption and high emission motor vehicles, vessels, and non-road mobile machinery, and reduces the consumption of fossil energy.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in areas where conditions permit, implement in advance the emission limits of the corresponding stage in the national motor vehicle air pollutant emission standards, and shall report to the competent department of ecological environment under the State Council for recordation.
City people's governments shall strengthen and improve urban traffic management, optimize road layout, and ensure the continuity and unimpeded flow of sidewalks and non-motor vehicle lanes.

Motor vehicles and vessels, and non-road mobile machinery shall not discharge atmospheric pollutants in excess of the standards.
The production, import or sale of motor vehicles and vessels, and non-road mobile machinery that discharge atmospheric pollutants in excess of the standards is prohibited.

Manufacturers of motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery shall conduct emission tests on newly manufactured motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery. Only those that pass the tests may be released for sale. The test information shall be made public to society.
The competent departments of ecological environment of the people's governments at or above the provincial level may strengthen supervision and inspection of the atmospheric pollutant emission status of newly manufactured and sold motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery by means of on-site inspection, sampling testing, etc. The relevant departments such as industry and market supervision and administration shall cooperate.

In-use motor vehicles shall undergo periodic emission tests by motor vehicle emission testing institutions in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State or local governments. Only those that pass the tests may be driven on roads. For those that do not pass the tests, the traffic management department of the public security organ shall not issue a safety technical inspection qualification mark.
The competent departments of ecological environment of the local people's governments at or above the county level may conduct supervision and spot tests on the atmospheric pollutant emission status of in-use motor vehicles at motor vehicle parking areas and maintenance sites; under the condition of not affecting normal traffic, they may conduct supervision and spot tests on the atmospheric pollutant emission status of motor vehicles running on roads through remote sensing monitoring and other technical means, and the traffic management department of the public security organ shall cooperate.

Motor vehicle emission testing institutions shall pass metrological accreditation according to law, use motor vehicle emission testing equipment that has been verified as qualified according to law, conduct emission tests on motor vehicles in accordance with the specifications formulated by the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, and connect with the competent department of ecological environment to achieve real-time sharing of test data. Motor vehicle emission testing institutions and their persons in charge shall be responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of the test data.
The competent departments of ecological environment and the certification and accreditation supervision and administration departments shall conduct supervision and inspection on the emission testing of motor vehicle emission testing institutions.

Motor vehicle production and import enterprises shall disclose to the public the emission test information, pollution control technology information, and relevant maintenance technical information of the motor vehicle models they produce or import.
Motor vehicle maintenance units shall, in accordance with the requirements for preventing and controlling atmospheric pollution and the relevant national technical specifications, maintain in-use motor vehicles so that they meet the prescribed emission standards. The competent departments of transport and ecological environment shall strengthen supervision and management according to law.
It is prohibited for motor vehicle owners to pass motor vehicle emission tests by fraudulent means such as temporarily replacing motor vehicle pollution control devices. It is prohibited for motor vehicle maintenance units to provide such maintenance services. It is prohibited to damage the on-board emission diagnostic system of motor vehicles.

The competent department of ecological environment shall, jointly with the relevant departments such as transport, housing and urban-rural construction, agricultural administration, and water administration, conduct supervision and inspection on the atmospheric pollutant emission status of non-road mobile machinery. Those with unqualified emissions shall not be used.

The State advocates environmentally friendly driving and encourages drivers of fuel motor vehicles to turn off the engine when it does not affect road traffic and parking is required for more than three minutes, so as to reduce the emission of atmospheric pollutants.

The State establishes a recall system for environmental protection of motor vehicles and non-road mobile machinery.
If a production or import enterprise learns that a motor vehicle or non-road mobile machinery discharges atmospheric pollutants in excess of the standards and this is due to a design or production defect or non-compliance with the prescribed environmental protection durability requirements, it shall recall such vehicles or machinery; if it fails to do so, the market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall, jointly with the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, order it to recall.

Where an in-use heavy-duty diesel vehicle or non-road mobile machinery is not equipped with a pollution control device, or the pollution control device does not meet the requirements, and it cannot meet the emission standards, it shall be retrofitted or replaced with a pollution control device that meets the requirements.

Where an in-use motor vehicle discharges atmospheric pollutants in excess of the standards, it shall be repaired; if after repair or the adoption of pollution control technology, the emission of atmospheric pollutants still does not comply with the national emission standards for in-use motor vehicles, it shall be compulsorily scrapped. Its owner shall sell the motor vehicle to a scrap motor vehicle recycling and dismantling enterprise, which shall carry out registration, dismantling, destruction and other treatment in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
The State encourages and supports the early scrapping of high-emission motor vehicles and vessels, and non-road mobile machinery.
The people's government of a city may, based on the atmospheric environmental quality conditions, delimit and publish areas where the use of high-emission non-road mobile machinery is prohibited.
Ship inspection institutions shall conduct emission tests on ship engines and related equipment. Only after passing the tests and meeting the national emission standards may the ship be operated.

Inland river and direct sea-river vessels shall use standard-compliant ordinary diesel. Ocean-going vessels shall, after berthing, use marine fuel that meets the requirements for atmospheric pollutant control.
Newly built wharves shall plan, design and construct shore-based power supply facilities; existing wharves shall gradually implement the renovation of shore-based power supply facilities. Vessels shall, after berthing, give priority to the use of shore power.

The competent department of transport of the State Council may, in coastal sea areas, designate ship atmospheric pollutant emission control zones. Vessels entering such emission control zones shall comply with the relevant ship emission requirements.

It is prohibited to produce, import, or sell fuels for motor vehicles and vessels, and non-road mobile machinery that do not meet the standards; it is prohibited to sell ordinary diesel or other non-motor vehicle fuels to automobiles and motorcycles; it is prohibited to sell residual oil and heavy oil to non-road mobile machinery, inland river vessels, and direct sea-river vessels.

The content of hazardous substances and other atmospheric environmental protection indicators in engine oil, nitrogen oxide reducing agents, fuel and lubricant additives, and other additives shall meet the requirements of the relevant standards, and shall not impair the effectiveness and durability of pollution control devices of motor vehicles and vessels, nor shall they add new emissions of atmospheric pollutants.

The State actively promotes the prevention and control of atmospheric pollution from civil aircraft and encourages the adoption of effective measures during the design, production, and use processes to reduce emissions of atmospheric pollutants.
Civil aircraft shall comply with the relevant engine emission requirements in the airworthiness standards prescribed by the State.

Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the management of construction and transportation, keep roads clean, control the stacking of materials and debris, expand the area of green spaces, water surfaces, wetlands, and ground paving, and prevent and control dust pollution.
The relevant departments such as housing and urban-rural construction, city appearance and environmental sanitation, transport, and land and resources shall, in accordance with the duties determined by the people's government at the corresponding level, carry out the work of preventing and controlling dust pollution.

A construction unit shall include the cost of preventing and controlling dust pollution in the project cost, and specify in the construction contract the responsibility of the construction contractor for preventing and controlling dust pollution. The construction contractor shall formulate a specific implementation plan for preventing and controlling dust pollution during construction.
Construction contractors engaged in housing construction, municipal infrastructure construction, river channel regulation, and building demolition shall file with the competent department responsible for supervising and managing dust pollution prevention and control.
A construction contractor shall set up hard enclosures at the construction site and take effective dust prevention and reduction measures such as covering, phased operation, time-appropriate construction, water spraying for dust suppression, and washing of the ground and vehicles. Excavated earth, engineering debris, and construction waste shall be promptly removed; if stored on site, they shall be covered with airtight dust-proof nets. Engineering debris and construction waste shall be treated for resource utilization.
A construction contractor shall disclose at the construction site information such as dust pollution prevention and control measures, the person in charge, and the competent department for dust supervision and management.
For construction land that cannot be started temporarily, the construction unit shall cover the exposed ground; if it exceeds three months, greening, paving, or covering shall be carried out.

Vehicles transporting bulk or fluid materials such as coal, garbage, debris, sand and gravel, earth, and mortar shall take measures such as sealing or other measures to prevent material spillage from causing dust pollution, and shall travel along prescribed routes.
Loading and unloading of materials shall adopt measures such as sealing or spraying to prevent dust pollution.
The people's government of a city shall strengthen the management of cleaning and maintenance of roads, squares, parking lots, and other public places, and promote low-dust operation methods such as mechanized cleaning with clean power to prevent and control dust pollution.

For municipal rivers and the exposed ground along river banks, public land, and other exposed urban ground, the relevant departments shall, in accordance with the plan, organize the implementation of greening or permeable paving.

Storage of coal, coal gangue, coal slag, coal ash, cement, lime, gypsum, sand and earth, and other materials prone to dust generation shall be enclosed; if enclosure is not possible, tight enclosures not lower than the height of the stacked materials shall be set up, and effective covering measures shall be taken to prevent dust pollution.
Wharves, mines, landfills, and disposal sites shall implement zoning operations and take effective measures to prevent dust pollution.

Local people's governments at all levels shall promote the transformation of agricultural production methods, develop agricultural circular economy, increase support for comprehensive treatment of waste, and strengthen the control of atmospheric pollutant emissions from agricultural production and operation activities.

Agricultural producers and operators shall improve fertilization methods, apply chemical fertilizers scientifically and rationally, and use pesticides in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, so as to reduce emissions of atmospheric pollutants such as ammonia and volatile organic compounds.
It is prohibited to spray highly toxic or highly poisonous pesticides on trees and flowers in densely populated areas.

Livestock and poultry farms and breeding communities shall promptly collect, store, transport, and conduct harmless treatment of sewage, livestock and poultry manure and carcasses, so as to prevent the emission of malodorous gases.

People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments such as agricultural administration shall encourage and support the adoption of advanced and applicable technologies for the comprehensive utilization of crop stalks and fallen leaves as fertilizer, feed, energy, industrial raw materials, and edible fungus substrates, and increase financial subsidies for agricultural machinery integrating stalk returning to the field and collection.
The people's government at the county level shall organize the establishment of a service system for the collection, storage, transportation, and comprehensive utilization of crop stalks, and adopt financial subsidies and other measures to support rural collective economic organizations, specialized farmer cooperative economic organizations, enterprises, etc. in carrying out services for the collection, storage, transportation, and comprehensive utilization of crop stalks.

The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall designate areas where open burning of crop stalks, fallen leaves, and other substances that produce smoke and dust pollution is prohibited.

The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, jointly with the health administration department of the State Council, publish a list of toxic and hazardous atmospheric pollutants and implement risk management based on the degree of harm and impact of atmospheric pollutants on public health and the ecological environment.
Enterprises and public institutions that discharge toxic and hazardous atmospheric pollutants listed in the list prescribed in the preceding paragraph shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, establish an environmental risk early warning system, conduct regular monitoring of discharge outlets and the surrounding environment, assess environmental risks, investigate environmental safety hazards, and take effective measures to prevent environmental risks.

Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and operators that discharge persistent organic pollutants into the atmosphere, as well as operating units of waste incineration facilities, shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, adopt technical methods and processes that are conducive to reducing emissions of persistent organic pollutants, equip with effective purification devices, and achieve emission compliance.

Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and operators that generate malodorous gases in production and operation activities shall scientifically select sites, set reasonable protection distances, and install purification devices or take other measures to prevent the emission of malodorous gases.

Operators of catering services that discharge cooking fumes shall install fume purification facilities and keep them in normal use, or take other fume purification measures to ensure that cooking fumes are discharged in compliance with standards, and prevent pollution to the normal living environment of nearby residents.
It is prohibited to newly build, rebuild, or expand catering service projects that produce cooking fumes, odors, or waste gases within residential buildings, commercial-residential mixed-use buildings that are not equipped with dedicated smoke ducts, and commercial floors adjacent to residential floors within commercial-residential mixed-use buildings.
No unit or individual shall engage in open-air barbecue or provide venues for open-air barbecue in areas where the local people's government prohibits such activities.

It is prohibited to burn asphalt, asphalt felt, rubber, plastic, leather, garbage, and other substances that produce toxic and harmful smoke and malodorous gases in densely populated areas and other areas requiring special protection according to law.
It is prohibited to produce, sell, or set off fireworks and firecrackers that do not meet quality standards. No unit or individual shall set off fireworks and firecrackers during periods or in areas prohibited by the people's government of a city.

The State encourages and advocates civilized and green sacrificial practices.
Crematoria shall install dust removal and other pollution prevention facilities and keep them in normal use to prevent impact on the surrounding environment.

Operators engaged in service activities such as garment dry cleaning and motor vehicle maintenance shall, in accordance with the relevant national standards or requirements, install odor and waste gas treatment devices and other pollution prevention facilities and keep them in normal use to prevent impact on the surrounding environment.

The State encourages and supports the production and use of alternatives to ozone-depleting substances, and gradually reduces until stops the production and use of ozone-depleting substances.
The State implements total quantity control and quota management for the production, use, import and export of ozone-depleting substances. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.

The State establishes a joint prevention and control mechanism for air pollution in key regions to coordinate and integrate the work of preventing and controlling air pollution in key regions. The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, based on the main functional area planning, regional atmospheric environmental quality status, and the patterns of atmospheric pollution transmission and diffusion, designate national key regions for air pollution prevention and control, and report to the State Council for approval.
The relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in key regions shall designate a lead local people's government, regularly hold joint meetings, and carry out joint prevention and control of air pollution in accordance with the requirements of unified planning, unified standards, unified monitoring, and unified prevention and control measures, and implement the target responsibilities for air pollution prevention and control. The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall strengthen guidance and supervision.
Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, by reference to the provisions of the first paragraph, designate key regions for air pollution prevention and control within their respective administrative areas.

The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council and the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in the national key regions for air pollution prevention and control, formulate an action plan for joint prevention and control of air pollution in key regions based on the economic and social development and atmospheric environmental carrying capacity of the key regions, specify control targets, optimize regional economic layout, coordinate traffic management, develop clean energy, and propose key prevention and control tasks and measures, so as to promote the improvement of atmospheric environmental quality in the key regions.

The comprehensive economic department of the State Council shall, jointly with the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council, further raise the requirements for environmental protection, energy consumption, safety, quality, etc., taking into account the actual industrial development and atmospheric environmental quality status of the national key regions for air pollution prevention and control.
The relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in key regions shall implement stricter emission standards for atmospheric pollutants from motor vehicles, unify the inspection methods and emission limits for in-use motor vehicles, and ensure the supply of qualified vehicle fuel.

The preparation of plans for industrial parks, development zones, regional industries and development, etc., that may cause serious pollution to the atmospheric environment of the national key regions for air pollution prevention and control, shall conduct environmental impact assessments according to law. The plan preparation authority shall consult with the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in the key regions or relevant departments.
Where the relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in key regions construct projects that may have a significant impact on the atmospheric environmental quality of neighboring provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, they shall promptly notify the relevant information and conduct consultations.
The consultation opinions and their adoption status shall serve as an important basis for the review or approval of environmental impact assessment documents.

Where a coal-using project is newly built, rebuilt, or expanded within a national key region for air pollution prevention and control, the equivalent or reduced substitution of coal shall be implemented.

The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall organize the establishment of a relevant information sharing mechanism for atmospheric environmental quality monitoring and atmospheric pollution source monitoring in the national key regions for air pollution prevention and control, use new technologies such as monitoring, simulation, satellite, aerial survey, and remote sensing to analyze the sources of atmospheric pollution in the key regions and their changing trends, and disclose such information to the public.

The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council and the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in the national key regions for air pollution prevention and control may organize relevant departments to carry out joint law enforcement, cross-regional law enforcement, and interleaved law enforcement.

The State establishes a monitoring and early warning system for heavy pollution weather.
The competent department of ecological environment of the State Council shall, jointly with the meteorological administration of the State Council and other relevant departments, and the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in the national key regions for air pollution prevention and control, establish a monitoring and early warning mechanism for heavy pollution weather in key regions, and unify the classification standards for early warnings. If heavy pollution weather may occur in a region, they shall promptly notify the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in the key regions.
The competent departments of ecological environment of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and cities divided into districts, shall, jointly with the meteorological authorities and other relevant departments, establish a monitoring and early warning mechanism for heavy pollution weather in their respective administrative areas.

Local people's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate the response to heavy pollution weather into the emergency management system for sudden events.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, cities divided into districts, and county people's governments where heavy pollution weather may occur, shall formulate emergency plans for heavy pollution weather, file them with the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at the next higher level, and make them public.

The competent departments of ecological environment of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and cities divided into districts, shall, jointly with the meteorological authorities, establish a consultation mechanism to conduct atmospheric environmental quality forecasting. If heavy pollution weather may occur, they shall promptly report to the people's government at the corresponding level. The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and cities divided into districts, shall, based on the heavy pollution weather forecast information, conduct comprehensive analysis and judgment, determine the early warning level, and issue early warnings in a timely manner. The early warning level shall be adjusted in a timely manner according to changes in circumstances. No unit or individual shall release heavy pollution weather forecast and early warning information to the public without authorization.
After the early warning information is released, the people's government and its relevant departments shall inform the public through television, radio, the internet, text messages, and other means to take health protection measures, guide the public in travel, and adjust other related social activities.

Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on the early warning level of heavy pollution weather, promptly initiate emergency plans, and may, according to emergency needs, take emergency measures such as ordering relevant enterprises to suspend or limit production, restricting the travel of some motor vehicles, prohibiting the setting off of fireworks and firecrackers, stopping earthwork and building demolition construction, stopping open-air barbecue, stopping outdoor activities organized by kindergartens and schools, and organizing and carrying out weather modification operations.
After the emergency response ends, the people's government shall promptly conduct an assessment of the implementation of the emergency plan and revise and improve the emergency plan as appropriate.

When a sudden environmental incident causing atmospheric pollution occurs, the people's government and its relevant departments and relevant enterprises and public institutions shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China and the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, properly carry out emergency response work. The competent department of ecological environment shall promptly monitor the atmospheric pollutants generated by the sudden environmental incident and make the monitoring information public.

In violation of the provisions of this Law, refusing to accept supervision and inspection by the competent department of ecological environment and its environmental law enforcement organs or other departments responsible for the supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection by means such as refusing to enter the site, or practicing fraud during supervision and inspection, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level or other departments responsible for the supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection shall order correction and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 101: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, produces, imports, sells or uses equipment or products prohibited in the National Comprehensive Industrial Policy Catalogue, adopts processes prohibited in the National Comprehensive Industrial Policy Catalogue, or transfers eliminated equipment or products to others for use, the economic comprehensive department of the people's government at or above the county level or the Customs shall, within their respective functions, order rectification, confiscate illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the value of the goods; if the party refuses to rectify, the matter shall be reported to the people's government with approval authority for approval, and the party shall be ordered to suspend business or close down. If the import constitutes smuggling, the Customs shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 102: Where a coal mine, in violation of this Law, fails to build supporting coal washing and processing facilities as required, the energy administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan; if the party refuses to rectify, the matter shall be reported to the people's government with approval authority for approval, and the party shall be ordered to suspend business or close down.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, mines coal containing radioactive substances, arsenic, or other toxic and hazardous substances exceeding the prescribed standards, the people's government at or above the county level shall, within the authority prescribed by the State Council, order the suspension of business or closure.

Article 105: Where a unit, in violation of this Law, burns coal or petroleum coke that does not meet quality standards, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the value of the goods.

Article 106: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, uses fuel for vessels that does not meet standards or requirements, the maritime administrative agency or the competent fisheries department shall, within their respective functions, impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 107: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, constructs or expands a facility burning high-pollution fuel within a designated no-burning zone, or fails to stop burning high-pollution fuel as required, or constructs or expands decentralized coal-fired heating boilers in areas covered by a centralized heating supply network, or fails to remove existing coal-fired heating boilers that cannot meet emission standards as required, the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the county level shall confiscate the facilities burning high-pollution fuel, organize the removal of the coal-fired heating boilers, and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, produces, imports, sells or uses boilers that do not meet the prescribed standards or requirements, the market supervision and administrative department or the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, confiscate illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Article 109: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, produces motor vehicles or non-road mobile machinery that exceed pollutant emission standards, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order rectification, confiscate illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the value of the goods, and confiscate and destroy the motor vehicles or non-road mobile machinery that cannot meet pollutant emission standards; if the party refuses to rectify, it shall be ordered to suspend production for remediation, and the competent department of motor vehicle production under the State Council shall order the cessation of production of that model.

Where a motor vehicle or non-road mobile machinery manufacturer, in violation of this Law, engages in fraud or passes off defective products as good ones regarding engines or pollution control devices, and passes off products as meeting emission inspection standards for sale, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order suspension of production for remediation, confiscate illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the value of the goods, and confiscate and destroy the motor vehicles or non-road mobile machinery that cannot meet pollutant emission standards, and the competent department of motor vehicle production under the State Council shall order the cessation of production of that model.

Article 110: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, imports or sells motor vehicles or non-road mobile machinery that exceed pollutant emission standards, the market supervision and administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level or the Customs shall, within their respective functions, confiscate illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the value of the goods, and confiscate and destroy the motor vehicles or non-road mobile machinery that cannot meet pollutant emission standards; if the import constitutes smuggling, the Customs shall impose a penalty according to law.

Where any motor vehicle or non-road mobile machinery sold, in violation of this Law, does not meet pollutant emission standards, the seller shall be liable for repair, replacement, or return of the goods; if losses are caused to the buyer, the seller shall compensate for the losses.

Article 111: Where a motor vehicle production or import enterprise, in violation of this Law, fails to publicly disclose emission inspection information or pollution control technology information for the motor vehicle models it produces or imports as required, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.

Where a motor vehicle production or import enterprise, in violation of this Law, fails to publicly disclose relevant maintenance technical information for the motor vehicle models it produces or imports as required, the competent department of transport of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 112: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, forges emission inspection results of motor vehicles or non-road mobile machinery or issues false emission inspection reports, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level shall confiscate illegal gains and impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the department responsible for qualification accreditation shall revoke its inspection qualification.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, forges emission inspection results of vessels or issues false emission inspection reports, the maritime administrative agency shall impose a penalty according to law.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, passes motor vehicle emission inspection by fraudulent means such as temporarily replacing pollution control devices, or damages the on-board emission diagnostic system of a motor vehicle, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, impose a fine of 5,000 yuan on the motor vehicle owner, and impose a fine of 5,000 yuan per vehicle on the motor vehicle repair unit.

Article 113: Where a motor vehicle driver, in violation of this Law, drives a motor vehicle that fails emission inspection on the road, the traffic administrative department of the public security organ shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 114: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, uses non-road mobile machinery that fails emission standards, or fails to install or replace pollution control devices on in-use heavy-duty diesel vehicles or non-road mobile machinery as required, the competent department of ecological environment and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions, order rectification and impose a fine of 5,000 yuan.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, uses high-emission non-road mobile machinery in an area where such use is prohibited, the competent department of ecological environment and other relevant departments of the people's government of the city shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 115: Where a construction unit, in violation of this Law, commits any of the following acts, the competent department of housing and urban-rural construction and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions, order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if the party refuses to rectify, it shall be ordered to suspend work for remediation:
(1) The construction site is not provided with hard enclosures, or effective dust prevention and reduction measures such as covering, sectional operation, timing of construction, water sprinkling to suppress dust, and washing of ground and vehicles are not taken;
(2) Construction earthwork, engineering spoil, and construction waste are not promptly removed, or are not covered with airtight dust-proof nets.

Where a construction project owner, in violation of this Law, fails to cover exposed ground on construction land that cannot be commenced temporarily, or fails to green, pave, or cover exposed ground on construction land that cannot be commenced for more than three months, the competent department of housing and urban-rural construction and other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall impose a penalty in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 116: Where a vehicle transporting coal, garbage, slag, sand, earth, mortar, or other bulk or fluid materials, in violation of this Law, fails to take airtight or other measures to prevent spillage of materials, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if the party refuses to rectify, the vehicle shall not be allowed on the road.

Article 118: Where a catering service operator that emits cooking fumes, in violation of this Law, fails to install lampblack purification facilities, fails to use them properly, or fails to take other lampblack purification measures, and emits cooking fumes exceeding the emission standards, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan; if the party refuses to rectify, it shall be ordered to suspend business for remediation.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, constructs, expands, or renovates a catering service project that generates cooking fumes, odors, or waste gases in a residential building, a commercial-residential mixed-use building without a dedicated fume extraction flue, or on a commercial floor adjacent to a residential floor within a commercial-residential mixed-use building, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification; if the party refuses to rectify, the project shall be closed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, barbecue food in the open air during periods or in areas prohibited by the local people's government, or provides venues for open-air barbecue, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification, confiscate barbecue tools and illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than 500 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan.

Article 119: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, sprays highly toxic or highly hazardous pesticides on trees, flowers, or grass in densely populated areas, or burns straw, fallen leaves, or other materials that produce smoke and dust pollution in the open air, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and may impose a fine of not less than 500 yuan but not more than 2,000 yuan.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, burns asphalt, linoleum, rubber, plastic, leather, garbage, or other materials that produce toxic and hazardous smoke and malodorous gases in densely populated areas or other areas requiring special protection according to law, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the people's government at the county level shall order rectification, impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan on the unit, and impose a fine of not less than 500 yuan but not more than 2,000 yuan on the individual.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, sets off fireworks or firecrackers during periods or in areas prohibited by the city people's government, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall impose a penalty according to law.

Article 120: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, engages in service activities such as garment dry cleaning or motor vehicle repair without installing pollution prevention facilities such as odor and waste gas treatment devices and keeping them in normal use, thereby affecting the surrounding environment, the competent department of ecological environment of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if the party refuses to rectify, it shall be ordered to suspend business for remediation.

Article 121: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, without authorization, releases heavy pollution weather forecast or early warning information to the public, which constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a penalty according to law.

Where anyone, in violation of this Law, refuses to implement emergency measures for heavy pollution weather such as suspending earthwork on construction sites or building demolition, the supervisory and administrative department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan.

Article 122: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, causes an air pollution accident, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level shall impose a fine in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of this Article; the directly responsible persons in charge and other directly liable persons may be fined not more than 50% of the income they received from the enterprise or institution in the preceding year.

For causing a general or relatively major air pollution accident, the fine shall be calculated at not less than one time but not more than three times the direct losses caused by the pollution accident; for causing a major or extraordinarily serious air pollution accident, the fine shall be calculated at not less than three times but not more than five times the direct losses caused by the pollution accident.

Article 124: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, retaliates against a whistleblower by terminating or modifying a labor contract or by other means, such person shall bear liability in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.
Article 125: Anyone who discharges air pollutants and causes harm shall bear tort liability according to law.

Article 126: Where any local people's government at any level, the competent department of ecological environment of the people's government at or above the county level, or any other department with supervisory and administrative responsibility for air environmental protection, or any of its staff members, abuses power, neglects duties, engages in favoritism or fraud, or falsifies information, disciplinary action shall be taken according to law.
Article 127: Where anyone, in violation of this Law, commits an act that constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 128: Prevention and control of air pollution from marine engineering projects shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.
Article 129: This Law shall come into force on January 1, 2016.
